section_summary: This section concerns Japanese overseas shortwave broadcasts and American monitoring of their propaganda. It includes consular reports, the Broadcasting Corporation of Japan’s June 1940 bulletin, and correspondence about American participation in a radio tribute to Prince Iyesato Tokugawa. The final pages contain the embassy’s record of that broadcast; Viscount Inouye’s speech continues beyond this section.

subfiles.title: Japanese Short-Wave Radio Programs for Overseas Reception
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Boyce forwards an April program and suggests regular distribution to the Department.
subfiles.summary: Boyce describes the Broadcasting Corporation of Japan’s monthly program as evidence of propaganda directed at the United States and elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Proposed Reply on the Tokugawa Broadcast
subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs proposes approving Grew’s participation and advance submission of his remarks.
subfiles.summary: Draft language for the Department’s reply to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Invitation to Ambassador Grew to Join Tokugawa Tribute
subfiles.about: Grew requests instructions on joining a July 5 radio tribute to Prince Tokugawa.
subfiles.summary: He proposes personal remarks and offers to submit the text in advance.

subfiles.title: Approval of Grew’s Tokugawa Broadcast
subfiles.about: The Department approves Grew’s participation and notes plans for an NBC rebroadcast.
subfiles.summary: The Department welcomes an advance draft of Grew’s remarks.

subfiles.title: Tokugawa Broadcast Information for the Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: James Lawrence Fly, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.about: Welles forwards news of the planned tribute for rebroadcast arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Notification to the FCC concerning Grew’s invitation.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Broadcast Information
subfiles.about: The FCC acknowledges the June 22 notice about the Tokugawa broadcast.
subfiles.summary: The Commission thanks the Department for forwarding the information.

subfiles.title: Telephone Notice to NBC and FCC
subfiles.about: An official records telephone calls conveying the broadcast time to NBC and the FCC.
subfiles.summary: The telegram arrived too late for a pre-holiday letter.

subfiles.title: Grew’s Proposed Tokugawa Broadcast Text
subfiles.about: Grew submits his proposed July 5 tribute for departmental review.
subfiles.summary: The speech praises Prince Iyesato Tokugawa’s character, public service, friendship with Americans, and work for the Red Cross. It recounts his upbringing and introduces Viscount Tadashiro Inouye as the next speaker.

subfiles.title: Approval and Date Query for Grew’s Speech
subfiles.about: The Department approves the speech and questions its date for the London Red Cross conference.
subfiles.summary: Approval is accompanied by a suggested correction from 1939 to 1938.

subfiles.title: Corrections to Grew’s Broadcast Text
subfiles.about: Grew confirms the 1938 correction and supplies further changes to his speech.
subfiles.summary: Changes concern Tokugawa’s age, career description, and school.

subfiles.title: Japanese Short Wave Radio Broadcasting for Overseas Reception
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Boyce forwards the June 1940 broadcasting bulletin and highlights its propaganda content.
subfiles.summary: He points to the growth and reach of Japanese shortwave broadcasting, use of Nisei participants, and new transmissions for Hawaii and the Near East. He asks whether reporting should continue.

subfiles.title: Overseas Broadcast, No. 48: Fifth Anniversary Commemoration Edition
subfiles.from: Nippon Hoso Kyokai, Broadcasting Corporation of Japan
subfiles.about: The June bulletin promotes Japanese overseas broadcasting and publishes articles, listener letters, and transmission schedules.
subfiles.summary: This fifth-anniversary issue describes the corporation’s expanding foreign-language services, listener correspondence, and planned Hawaii and Near East transmissions. It presents Japanese culture, history, arts, science, Nisei education, and television experiments, alongside letters from listeners abroad. It gives detailed June programs and frequencies for audiences in North America, China, the South Seas, and the Dutch East Indies.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Obtain the Broadcasting Bulletin in Tokyo
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Stanley G. Slavens, American Consul, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department directs the Tokyo consul to send the bulletin regularly and comment on propaganda features.
subfiles.summary: A single copy is requested if obtainable without cost.

subfiles.title: No Action on Kabayama Broadcast Notice
subfiles.about: An official notes that notice arrived after Count Kabayama’s scheduled U.S. broadcast.

subfiles.title: Notice of Count Kabayama’s Broadcast
subfiles.about: Grew reports Kabayama’s forthcoming Columbia network talk on Japanese-American relations.
subfiles.summary: The telegram specifies the planned Tokyo broadcast time.

subfiles.title: A Tribute to the Late Prince Iyesato Tokugawa
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew transmits the texts of his and Inouye’s July 5 radio tributes.
subfiles.summary: The despatch places both broadcast speeches in the Department’s records.

subfiles.title: Grew’s Broadcast Tribute to Prince Iyesato Tokugawa
subfiles.about: Grew memorializes Tokugawa’s public service and support for Japanese-American friendship.
subfiles.summary: The final text incorporates the corrections discussed in July telegrams. Grew recalls Tokugawa’s leadership, Red Cross service, personal qualities, and friendship with Americans before introducing Inouye.

subfiles.title: Inouye’s Broadcast Tribute to Prince Tokugawa
subfiles.about: Inouye begins a tribute to Tokugawa’s character, lineage, and family history.
